title: West Yorkshire Police's first live facial recognition deployment in Huddersfield: three arrests, including a domestic stalking suspect, and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks over three days
summary: West Yorkshire Police reported three arrests and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks after NEC NeoFace live facial recognition issued nine alerts in Huddersfield on 12 to 14 August 2026.
account: The National Physical Laboratory tested NEC NeoFace V4 for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police in 2022 and reported in March 2023. It found that at a face-match threshold of 0.64 the system produced no false positives and had a true recognition rate of 79 percent. West Yorkshire Police records the same threshold of 0.64 for its deployments. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system and states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield from 12 to 14 August 2026. The force reported three arrests, involving a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant and a shoplifting suspect. It also reported six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on 12 August and two on each following day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951 and 4,100, which total 12,875. These figures come from the force's own operational records, and no source reports an independent study of these deployments. The absence of recorded false alerts does not establish that the system missed no matches. The reported arrests and checks do not establish a conviction or a specific harm that was prevented. The force's register shows that the vans returned to Huddersfield town center on 8, 9 and 10 September 2026, with 16 alerts, all confirmed true. They returned again on 10 October 2026 and recorded no alerts.
purpose: Live facial recognition vans are deployed to match passersby against a watchlist of wanted people and suspects so that officers can arrest or check them. The arrests and order checks are that purpose. The Examiner adds that the cameras also serve to find missing people, witnesses and victims.
system: NEC NeoFace live facial recognition used in West Yorkshire Police camera vans

fields.title: West Yorkshire Police's first live facial recognition deployment in Huddersfield: three arrests, including a domestic stalking suspect, and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks over three days
fields.headline: Police facial recognition vans in Huddersfield lead to three arrests

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public record and its assessments

provenance.basis: SHA-256 of the public record, its assessments, and its displayed answers and notes, excluding its own identifier and the derived coverage summary.

fields.account: The National Physical Laboratory tested NEC NeoFace V4 for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police in 2022 and reported in March 2023. It found that at a face-match threshold of 0.64 the system produced no false positives and had a true recognition rate of 79 percent. West Yorkshire Police records the same threshold of 0.64 for its deployments. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system and states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield from 12 to 14 August 2026. The force reported three arrests, involving a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant and a shoplifting suspect. It also reported six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on 12 August and two on each following day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951 and 4,100, which total 12,875. These figures come from the force's own operational records, and no source reports an independent study of these deployments. The absence of recorded false alerts does not establish that the system missed no matches. The reported arrests and checks do not establish a conviction or a specific harm that was prevented. The force's register shows that the vans returned to Huddersfield town center on 8, 9 and 10 September 2026, with 16 alerts, all confirmed true. They returned again on 10 October 2026 and recorded no alerts.
